sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the Midrashic parable of three crowns for the King, and the two interpretations regarding which verses correspond to the two crowns given to Israel.

translations.translation: And it continues in
(the explanation of)
the maamar,
that this is what is stated in the Midrash
(regarding the three times "Kadosh"),
a parable of the citizens of a province who made three crowns for the king.
What did the king do?
He placed one on his own head and two on the heads of his sons.
So too, every day the supernal beings crown the Holy One, blessed be He, with three sanctifications.
What does the Holy One, blessed be He, do?
He places one on His head and two on the heads of Israel.
As the verse states,
"For I am holy, and you shall sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy."
That is, "For I am holy" is the crown He places on His head,
and "you shall sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy" are the two crowns He placed on the heads of Israel.
And it is noteworthy,
that in the Midrash before us it states the verse: "Speak to the entire congregation of the children of Israel: You shall be holy, and you shall sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy,"
for ostensibly from this it implies that the two crowns placed on the heads of Israel are "You shall be holy"
(which is adjacent to "For I am holy")
and "you shall sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy"
(which are both considered one crown).
But in Likkutei Torah it explains
that the two crowns placed on the heads of Israel are "you shall sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy,"
and "You shall be holy"
(which is adjacent to "For I am holy")
is not counted among the crowns.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the Midrashic statement that "Your holiness is above your holiness" and the Tzemach Tzedek's difficulty, resolved by Likkutei Torah distinguishing holiness through mitzvos from the higher holiness drawn by teshuvah.

translations.translation: And this can be explained based on what is stated in the Midrash there,
"You shall be holy" — perhaps [you could be] like Me? The Torah says, "For I am holy" — My holiness is above your holiness.
My holiness is above your holiness.
And the Tzemach Tzedek wrote
(in Ohr HaTorah, beginning of Parshat K'doshim)
that this is perplexing.
And the intention in this
(simply)
is,
for how is it even conceivable that Israel could be like Me?
And in Likkutei Torah, Parshat Nitzavim,
it is explained,
that "your holiness" is the holiness drawn through arousal from below of the performance of mitzvos,
and "My holiness" which is above your holiness is a most elevated holiness that the arousal from below of the performance of mitzvos does not reach there,
and it is drawn through teshuvah.
And this is why baalei teshuvah are higher than completely righteous individuals,
for through teshuvah they draw from the aspect of "My holiness" which is above "your holiness,"
as explained in Likkutei Torah there.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions how the higher holiness of "Kadosh Ani" can be drawn downward, contrasting the approach of the completely righteous with that of baalei teshuvah, and notes the apparent contradiction between Ohr HaTorah and Likkutei Torah.

translations.translation: And ostensibly it must be said,
that the superiority of baalei teshuvah over completely righteous individuals,
even though among the righteous there is also the service of the three times "Kadosh" and the first "Kadosh" is "Kadosh Ani"
("My holiness is above your holiness"),
is,
that the revelation of the first "Kadosh" among the righteous is in a manner of ascent upward,
that they yearn to depart from their existence and be included in His holiness, may He be blessed
(and that which is drawn to them while they are below is only the second and third "Kadosh"),
and among baalei teshuvah,
even the first "Kadosh" is in a manner of drawing downward.
And it must be understood,
how is it possible for the holiness of "Kadosh Ani" to be drawn downward?
And even more so it is not understood,
for in Ohr HaTorah it is stated,
that even the possibility that they could be like Me is perplexing,
and in Likkutei Torah it is stated
(even according to the conclusion),
that through teshuvah they draw the holiness of "Kadosh Ani,"
for ostensibly these are contradictory notions.
